_doc: Voiceover, one entry per clip. 'at' is the earliest start in seconds from the scene start; lines in a scene never overlap (each waits for the previous one plus a short gap). Regenerate with scripts/voiceover.py after editing.

Flip.text: For years, robots have learned by copying us.
Now the robot teaches, and you learn.

Why.text: Why a robot? It knows every joint angle exactly. It never gets tired, and it never judges you.

Virtual.text: One problem: we couldn't get access to a real robot here.
So we built a virtual dojo, with real physics.

ArmDemo.text: We started small: a robot hand, teaching sign language.
It shows a sign, you copy it, and every finger gets checked.
And it's honest. When four fingers can't make the real sign, it tells you.

UnitreeDemo.text: This is a real run at our table: a Unitree G1, teaching kung fu.
See the red? It tells you exactly which limb to fix.
Every limb green, hold for three seconds, and you've passed.

Trick.text: But the robot is shorter than you. So is that fair?
We turn both bodies into the same eight arrows.
We ignore their length, and only compare which way they point.
The biggest miss becomes one simple tip.

Stack.text: Under the hood: MuJoCo, MediaPipe, our own stance recogniser, and Nebius for the AI sensei.

Limits.text: To be honest: the robots are virtual for now, and the stances are set by hand.

Next.text: You get it wrong, and it walks over, and gently moves your arm into place.

Close.text: Robots spent years learning from us.
Now, they can teach us back.

direction: Talk like a real person telling a friend about something you built today and are proud of: warm, relaxed, conversational, with natural pauses and a little smile in your voice. Not an announcer, not an advert.
